prompt: A published case is negative in every single year and reports the status no-sign-change. Why does no rate exist for it?
options: The search runs from -99 to 1000 percent, and a loss this deep needs a rate somewhere under the floor of that band, which the engine declines to report.
Discounting shrinks every year by the same factor, so a flow whose years all point one way keeps that sign at every rate the search visits.
A rate needs at least three producing years to solve against, and a case with no positive year offers nothing to iterate on.
The engine refuses to price a flow it cannot verify, so the status stands in place of the rate and of the value.
explanation: Raising the rate on a flow that only spends makes the loss smaller and never reaches zero; the case that only spends is worth -524.1537.

prompt: The published zero capex case is worth 717.9604 and reports no-sign-change. What does that status say about the case?
options: It was priced before its capex was entered, so the 717.9604 is a partial result the engine will revise once a capex field carries a figure.
It is the strongest of the published cases, since a flow positive in every year carries a rate somewhere above the clamp of 1000 percent.
It failed a completeness check, since a concept with no capex at all is refused by name and returns no value a reader can use.
It never asked for money up front, so there is no investment for a return to be a return on.
explanation: Four of the five no-sign-change cases lose money and this one makes it, and none of the five carries a rate; the 717.9604 is the whole answer.

prompt: All five published no-sign-change cases withhold a rate. Which figure still reads for every one of them?
options: The net present value, which is defined for any cash flow at any discount rate and is stated in money rather than in percent.
The payback, which is recorded as the project life whenever the cumulative offers the engine no crossing at all to measure against.
The rate at the floor of the band, -99 percent, which is what a bounded search reports whenever it finds no crossing above that floor.
The status alone, since a case with no rate carries no value either and only the reason survives.
explanation: On the case with royalty at 100 percent the value of -1464.8989 is the whole story: the state took the gross revenue and the contractor carried the costs.

prompt: One published no-sign-change case records a rate of 0 and a payback equal to the project life, on a value of -979.6325. What is that 0?
options: A solved root, since a flow with no production crosses zero at the origin and the search confirms it there.
The floor of the reportable range, substituted for a null so that a screening card always carries a number.
A convention belonging to that published case, standing in for a flow with no revenue at all rather than reporting a root the engine solved and verified.
The rate the case would earn once production were restored, held as a placeholder until a profile is entered.
explanation: None of the five statuses means zero. A rate of 0 here answers a flow with no revenue, alongside a value of -979.6325 and a payback taken by convention.

prompt: The tiny capex case is worth 133.3087, its status is above-clamp, and the golden records a root of 15389.6875 percent. What is that status saying?
options: The rate is so large the engine treats it as an overflow and reports the clamp in place of a number nobody could reproduce.
No return exists for this case at all, and above-clamp is the status used when a search leaves the band without a root.
The value of 133.3087 is too small for a root to be resolved against it, so the golden carries what the engine declines to state.
A root exists and it sits above the 1000 percent top of the band the engine searched.
explanation: Reporting a root it did not find is how a card ends up carrying a number nobody can reproduce; the second such case reads 2305.7875 on a value of 1074.4692.

prompt: How can a case worth only 133.3087 carry a root of 15389.6875 percent?
options: The root compounds across the whole project life, so a value as small as 133.3087 spread over the twenty years of the profile reaches four figures of percent.
The rate divides out scale: a very small outlay followed by a large single year needs an enormous rate to shrink the receipt back down to the outlay.
The value was struck at 10.0000 percent and the root at the top of the band, and the gap between the two rates is the difference.
The case earns its whole return in one year, and a rate measured on a single year is multiplied by the years the flow leaves unused.
explanation: The money stays small at 133.3087 while the ratio explodes; the second above-clamp case is three fat years on a capex of 20 at 2305.7875 percent.

prompt: A screening case comes back above-clamp. What is the first thing to check?
options: The band, which should be widened until the root appears so that 15389.6875 percent can be carried onto the management page.
The value, since a case above the clamp is a marginal one and belongs with the failures until its rate can be stated properly.
The capex, since a case clearing 1000 percent usually has one that is wrong, missing or entered in the wrong units.
The discount rate, since a root above the band means the case was struck at a rate too low for the shape the concept implies.
explanation: A real development case sits far inside the band: every rate that zeroes an EGINA flow falls between -66.9344 and 43.8661 percent, so a four figure root is a prompt about the inputs.

prompt: Three of the five statuses withhold a rate for three different reasons. Which reading of them is right?
options: no-sign-change says no root exists, above-clamp says a root exists above the band the search covers, and no-root says the flow changes sign and no rate inside the band zeroes it.
no-sign-change says the search ran out of iterations, above-clamp says the root sits at the edge of the band, and no-root says the value came out negative.
no-sign-change says the capex is missing, above-clamp says the capex is too small, and no-root says the price deck is shorter than the profile.
no-sign-change says the rate is zero, above-clamp says the rate is 1000 percent, and no-root says the rate is somewhere the engine will not name.
explanation: None of the three means zero and none of them is a rate. At 18.0000 USD a barrel the status is no-root on a value of -1834.1220 million USD.

prompt: The published case whose price deck stops before the profile does reports multiple-roots. Where does its second change of sign come from?
options: The last price in the deck is held flat to the end of the profile, and a flat price set against a steadily declining shape drags the late years under zero.
The missing prices are read as 0, so the uncovered years produce barrels at no price while still carrying their operating cost and turn negative again.
A second capex phase is inserted where the deck ends, so the flow spends again part way through its life and crosses zero once more.
The uncovered years are dropped from the profile entirely, which shortens the life below the point at which the cumulative had turned positive.
explanation: The flow goes down, then up, then down, so the curve touches zero twice; the case is worth 126.1636 and neither crossing has a claim to be the answer.

prompt: The golden for that shortened deck case records a root of -52.4425 percent. Why is that still not its rate of return?
options: Another root exists and is equally valid, so the case has no single rate at all and -52.4425 percent is one crossing of two.
It sits below the floor of the search at -99 percent, so the engine never visited that part of the band and the golden records it from outside.
A negative root is never reported as a rate by the engine, which is why the status names a refusal in place of carrying the number.
It was solved on the deck as entered rather than on the profile, so it describes a shorter case.
explanation: A negative root is unremarkable arithmetic; what gets a rate withheld is the shape of the flow, and this flow crosses zero more than once on a value of 126.1636.

prompt: At 30.0000 USD a barrel the concept reads no-root and at 70.0000 USD a barrel it reads multiple-roots. What is the difference between those two answers?
options: How far each value sits below zero, since a loss as shallow as -935.1995 still admits roots and a deeper one does not.
Whether a payback exists, since the case at 70.0000 USD a barrel pays back in 3.8273 years and the case at 30.0000 never does, which is what the two statuses record.
Which search was run, since multiple-roots comes from the band of -99 to 1000 percent and no-root from a second pass made outside that band.
Whether any rate zeroes the flow at all, since one crosses zero more than once and the other crosses nowhere the band reaches.
explanation: Reading the two as synonyms loses the finding: at 30.0000 USD a barrel no rate zeroes the flow at all, and at 70.0000 two do, on values of -935.1995 and 2015.4123.

prompt: In the studio's plan path a price deck that does not cover the profile is not padded. What happens instead?
options: The deck is extended at its last price and the case is priced, with the status carrying the extension so a reader can see it was made.
The uncovered years are priced at 0 and the case comes back multiple-roots, which is the signal to go back and finish the deck properly.
The case is refused by name: "the price deck has no price for production year 3: enter a price for every year of the profile".
The profile is truncated to the length of the deck and the case is priced over that shorter life, which is worth 126.1636.
explanation: Reading a missing price as 0 is what produces the second sign change; the plan path refuses instead, so no value is struck on a deck that stops early.

prompt: At 18.0000 USD a barrel the concept is worth -1834.1220 million USD. Before the repair the engine reported a rate there. What was the number, and what was it a property of?
options: 1000 percent, the top of its own search band, which is a property of the search and not of the cash flow it was run on.
1000 percent, the highest rate the flow reaches at any point in its life, verified before it was returned.
A null with no status, which readers filled in by hand because a card would not draw without a number.
The floor of -99 percent, since a loss this deep drives the search to the bottom of the band.
explanation: The flow does change sign, since year 0 spends 2250.0000 and later years earn, so a naive search starts looking and simply never finds a crossing.

prompt: The clamp of 1000 percent survived a long time on the cards. What made it so hard to notice?
options: It appeared only on cases the engine refused elsewhere as well, so the rate was never the number a reader was actually looking at on the card.
It moved with the price deck as a solved rate would, so no reader could tell it apart from the rates the engine reports on the cases that have one.
It cleared every threshold anyone would set, so it was coloured green on a case whose value of -1834.1220 million USD says the opposite.
It was printed with no status beside it, and the four statuses that name a refusal arrived only in the repair that removed the clamp.
explanation: Nothing about 1000 percent announces that it came from the boundary; the failure is silent, and the contradicting value was printed next to it the whole time.

prompt: What is the tell that a reported rate came from a boundary rather than from a solution?
options: It carries the status ok, which the repaired engine now keeps for a verified root and which the clamped search set on every single run it made.
It sits exactly on the limit of the search range, where the engine's genuine answers do not: -36.6747 percent on the published case, or the roots -44.3414 and 29.5779 on the plan's own.
It appears beside a payback of never, which is the pairing the repaired engine refuses and the clamped search produced freely.
It is printed to one decimal place while a solved root carries four, which is how a boundary can be spotted on a card.
explanation: A solver landing precisely on its own limit has returned a return code; the published tax floor case is the same shape at -944.3201 with the status no-root.
